messages.author: ce1869eaef9b2686
messages.subject: polychoric correlation with alternate forms
parts:
I want to do a polychoric correlation for binary scored data.  There were 2 test forms, A and B, which were randomly assigned to individuals. Supposing each form had 2 questions (they had 30 items each, I only use 2 for illustration), my data looks like the following, where Q1 and Q2 are form A and Q3 and Q4 are form B.  Each row represents a different individual.
  
Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4
1  0  NA NA
0  0  NA NA
1  1  NA NA
NA NA 1 0
NA NA 0 1
NA NA 0 0

I want to run the following model:
  
model <-'
eta =~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4
'

When I call:

fit <- cfa(model, data = Y,std.lv=T,missing='fiml',ordered=c("Q1","Q2","Q3","Q4")
summary(fit,fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

Error in eigen(S, symmetric = TRUE) : infinite or missing values in 'x'
In addition: Warning messages:
  1: In lav_options_set(opt) :  lavaan WARNING: information will be set to “expected” for se = “robust.sem”
2: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :  lavaan WARNING: some cases are empty and will be ignored:

The warning output (and the fitted model) indicate that only the first 3 rows (using the data example provided, above) are used and the 3 rows starting with NA are not used.  

If I pull the missing='fiml' option out, the result is still the same, where only the first 3 rows are used.  

Any suggestion on how I can make this work? It seems that lavaan is calling rows 4 through 6 complete missing data and not using them.  

Thanks.

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: polychoric correlation with alternate forms
parts:
This model is not identified. You don't have any data to inform the
correlations Q1 <-> Q3, Q2 <-> Q3, Q1 <-> Q4, Q2 <-> Q4. No matter how
hard you try, you won't get an identified model out of this.

Post mortem (see https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Ronald_Fisher, the last
item from 1930s): you should have had more forms with anchor items
among them.

messages.subject: Re: polychoric correlation with alternate forms
parts:
Good point--makes perfect sense, now that you mention it.  Yes, I have heard Fisher's post-mortem quote before; but I think this might be the first time I have experienced it.

So. I wonder if there might be some workaround? Maybe treat this as a 2 group analysis--one group received form A, another group received form B? There are no shared items; but people were randomly assigned to test form.  

Or specify the model in a different way maybe, such as perhaps creating a single latent variable and consider items from test form A and test form B as observations.

Something else? I'll keep thinking about it...

Thanks again.

Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: polychoric correlation with alternate forms
parts: You also cannot use FIML with categorical outcomes in lavaan.  ML assumes normal data, although continuous is sufficient because there are nonnormality corrections to SEs and tests (not sufficient for binary outcomes because those relationships will be underestimated, if the latent-response assumption holds).  So multiple imputation would be necessary to handle the missingness.

I wonder if there might be some workaround? Maybe treat this as a 2 group analysis--one group received form A, another group received form B? There are no shared items; but people were randomly assigned to test form.

Well, sufficient auxiliary information might be able to bail you out here, assuming strong correlations both with and among the latent responses underlying your binary items.  If there are other observed variables that are associated with both {Q1, Q2} and {Q3, Q4}, then an association between those forms might inferred indirectly, at least within reasonable bounds.  For instance, if A is correlated .7 with B and .8 with C, then there are certain logical boundaries for the B-C correlation, beyond which the correlation matrix would be NPD (impossible to observe).  Here is a Cudeck (200) paper that discusses this in the continuous case with covariances among items not jointly observed:

https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF02296344?LI=true

Not sure how pivotal the linearity and normality assumptions are, i.e., it might not work as well when imputing binary data because it won't draw on the simplifying normality assumption -- but I imagine the same principle applies to some degree.  But if it does not capture sufficient information to fit a factor model to those 4 items, that should be reflected in your pooled point and SE estimates.  Worth a try.  Check out the ?cfa.mi help page in the semTools package for help; there's a categorical example at the bottom.  Might want to download the development versions if you decide to use it:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/lavaan/Mz__T8_DlUM/gvyXApiIAgAJ

Good luck,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: polychoric correlation with alternate forms
parts:
Chris,
You options may also depend upon the nature of the two forms.  If your alternate forms are parallel only in the classical sense, same mean and error variance, then you have 60 variables and Terrence's suggestion might offer your best option.  If your alternative forms are parallel in the modern sense of following the same test specification so that there is a one-to-one pairing of items from the two forms, then you can treat this as a two-group measurement invariance analysis by reconfiguring the data to have 30 variables plus a group/form variable instead of 60.

Keith
------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/
